symptom: `describe Module.Name` reports `no describable document named "..."` for a document that plainly exists and that `describe building block Module.Name` / `describe icon collection Module.Name` describes fine when the type is named explicitly
cause: Two lists in different packages drifted apart. Bare DESCRIBE resolves the type by looking the qualified name up in the catalog `objects` view and mapping its `ObjectType` through `objectTypeToDescribeKind`. Building blocks were built into `building_blocks_data` but never joined into the `objects` view union, so the lookup returned no row; icon collections had **no catalog table at all**, leaving the `ICON_COLLECTION` entry in the map as dead code that nothing could ever emit. Measured on a stock 7-module marketplace project: 43 of 251 documents (40 building blocks + 3 icon collections) were unreachable this way — auto-detect coverage 81%, explicit-type coverage 98%
file: `mdl/executor/describe_auto.go` (`objectTypeToDescribeKind`), `mdl/catalog/tables.go` (the `objects` view union + the `*_data` table), `mdl/catalog/builder.go` (`buildSimpleNamedDocs` call), `mdl/catalog/catalog.go` (the `CATALOG.*` table list)
insight: Add the type in **all four** places — a map entry alone does nothing if the view never emits the `ObjectType`, and a view row alone does nothing if the map has no kind. For a document with just name/folder/documentation, the builder is one `buildSimpleNamedDocs("<Unit$Type>", "<table>", "<Label>")` line; get the unit `$Type` from the MPR itself (`Images$ImageCollection` vs `CustomIcons$CustomIconCollection`), not from the catalog, which only knows types it already models. **Do not measure coverage from the catalog** — the `objects` view indexes only describable types, so it reports 100% by construction; enumerate raw unit `$Type`s instead. Guard is `TestDescribeAutoCoversCatalogObjectTypes` in `mdl/executor/describe_auto_test.go`, which reads the `ObjectType` literals out of the view's own SQL and fails when one has neither a describe kind nor an entry in `notAutoDescribable`. Watch for **new ambiguity**: adding types to a name-keyed index can make a qualified name match two kinds (verified none here). Issue: marketplace-diff DESCRIBE coverage spike
